title: Person Recognition at Altitude and Range: Fusion of Face, Body Shape and Gait

AI.tldr: The paper presents FarSight, an end-to-end system for whole-body person recognition at long range that fuses face, gait and body shape cues, and reports large gains over the authors' preliminary system on the BRIAR benchmark.
AI.motivation: Biometric recognition in surveillance is hard when data is captured at long standoff distances, high elevation angles and under turbulence or wind, which degrades images and causes pose, scale and cross-domain gaps.
AI.method: FarSight combines four modules: multi-subject detection and tracking, recognition-aware video restoration, modality-specific biometric feature encoding for face, gait and body shape, and quality-guided multi-modal fusion.
AI.result: Compared with the preliminary system, FarSight achieves a 34.1% absolute gain in 1:1 verification accuracy (TAR@0.1% FAR), a 17.8% increase in closed-set identification (Rank-20) and a 34.3% reduction in open-set identification errors (FNIR@1% FPIR) on the BRIAR dataset; it was also evaluated in the 2025 NIST RTE Face in Video Evaluation (FIVE).
AI.conclusion: The authors position FarSight as a state-of-the-art solution for operational biometric recognition in challenging real-world conditions.

title: GenHOI: Generalizing Text-driven 4D Human-Object Interaction Synthesis for Unseen Objects

AI.tldr: The paper proposes GenHOI, a two-stage framework that synthesises text-driven 4D human-object interaction sequences for objects unseen in training, reaching state-of-the-art results on OMOMO and 3D-FUTURE.
AI.motivation: Text-driven 4D human-object interaction synthesis lags behind human motion synthesis because large-scale 4D HOI datasets are scarce, and existing methods do not generalise well to unseen objects.
AI.method: The first stage uses an Object-AnchorNet, trained only on 3D HOI datasets, to reconstruct sparse 3D HOI keyframes for unseen objects. The second stage uses a Contact-Aware Diffusion Model (ContactDM) with a Contact-Aware Encoder to extract human-object contact patterns and Contact-Aware HOI Attention to inject contact signals, interpolating the keyframes into dense, temporally coherent 4D sequences.
AI.result: The abstract reports state-of-the-art results on the public OMOMO and 3D-FUTURE datasets and strong generalisation to unseen objects, with high-fidelity 4D HOI generation; no specific numbers are given in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: GenHOI reduces dependence on large-scale 4D HOI data and generalises to unseen objects, which the authors present as a step toward high-fidelity 4D HOI synthesis.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Consecutive Preferential Bayesian Optimization (CPBO), which reuses the previous candidate in each pairwise comparison to cut production cost and models oracle indifference with a Just-Noticeable Difference threshold.
AI.motivation: Existing preferential Bayesian optimization ignores the cost of producing candidate solutions for evaluation, and it does not model the perceptual ambiguity of human feedback, which can be indifferent to small utility differences.
AI.method: CPBO uses a consecutive comparison setting in which each new candidate is compared against the previous one. It adds a Just-Noticeable Difference threshold to a probabilistic preference model and adapts an information-theoretic acquisition strategy that selects configurations most informative about the unknown optimum.
AI.result: The method shows a notable increase in accuracy in setups with high production costs or indifference feedback, and its practical feasibility is demonstrated on a real-world food extrusion task.
AI.conclusion: Accounting for production cost and perceptual ambiguity makes preferential optimisation more practical when candidates are expensive to produce or when human feedback is indifferent.

title: Why Is Dyck$_1$ Hard for Language Models? Learning and Generalizing a One-Counter Language.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how RNNs and Transformers learn and generalise the one-counter language Dyck-1 (balanced parentheses), finding strong depth and length generalisation despite formal expressivity limits, and identifying numerical sensitivity and length-by-range-of-dependence regions as predictors of failure.
AI.motivation: Formal proofs that RNNs and Transformers cannot recognise Dyck-1 rely on assumptions that do not carry over to practical settings, leaving a gap between theory and practice.
AI.method: The authors give a taxonomy of the assumptions behind theoretical and empirical claims and run controlled comparative experiments on learnability and generalisation in RNNs and Transformers with seven positional encodings.
AI.result: Both RNNs and Transformers show strong depth and length generalisation despite their formal inability to recognise Dyck-1 with unbounded precision; numerical sensitivity and jointly defined regions of length and range-of-dependence are identified as additional predictors of generalisation failure.
AI.conclusion: Human intuition may be a poor guide to what is algorithmically or mechanistically hard for neural networks.
